name: Fetch Behemoth

notes.saves: +1 status to all saves vs. magic

spells.name: Cataclysm
spells.text:
You call upon the unimaginable power of world-ending cataclysms, ripping a small piece of each cataclysm and combining them together into one horrifically powerful attack. The following effects come down upon all creatures in the area. Treat the resistances of creatures in the area as if they were 10 lower for the purpose of determining the cataclysm's damage. Each creature attempts one basic Reflex save that applies to all five types of damage.

- Flesh-dissolving acid rain deals 3d10 acid damage.

- A roaring earthquake shakes and bludgeons creatures on the ground, dealing 3d10 bludgeoning damage.

- A blast of freezing wind deals 3d10 cold damage.

- Incredible lightning lashes the area, dealing 3d10 electricity damage.

- Beating winds churn across the sky, dealing 3d10 bludgeoning damage to creatures flying in the area.

- An instant tsunami sweeps over creatures in the area, dealing 3d10 bludgeoning damage with the water trait (doubled for creatures swimming in the area).

- A massive wildfire burns in a sudden inferno, dealing 3d10 fire damage.

spells.name: Detonate Magic
spells.text: You cause the magic within the target to dissipate in a destructive explosion. You attempt to counteract the target. If the attempt succeeds, an explosion of magical force deals 8d6 force damage with a basic Reflex save. If you successfully counteract the magic of an item, it's deactivated for 1 week (or destroyed on a critical success) and the explosion is a 5-foot emanation from the item. If you successfully counteract a spell, the effect ends and the explosion affects either all creatures in the spell's area or the target of the spell and all creatures in a 5-foot emanation around it.

spells.name: Earthquake
spells.text:
You shake the ground, topple creatures into fissures, and collapse structures. The GM might add additional effects in certain areas. Cliffs might collapse, causing creatures to fall, or a lake might drain as fissures open up below its surface, leaving a morass of quicksand.
- Shaking Ground The ground is difficult terrain, and creatures on it take a -2 circumstance penalty to attack rolls, AC, and skill checks. Spell Effect: Earthquake (Shaking Ground)
- Fissures Each creature on the ground must attempt a Reflex save at the start of its turn to keep its footing and avoid falling into 40-foot-deep fissures that open beneath it. The fissures are permanent, and their sides require successful DC 15 Athletics check to Climb.
- Collapse Structures and ceilings might collapse. The GM rolls a flat check for each (DC 16 Flat check for a sturdy structure, DC 14 Flat check for an average structure and most natural formations, DC 9 Flat check for a shoddy structure, all adjusted higher or lower as the GM sees fit). A collapse deals 11d6 bludgeoning damage to each creature caught in it with a basic Reflex save. A creature falls Prone unless it critically succeeds and falls into a fissure if it critically fails.

---
Heightened (10th) You create a massive earthquake that can devastate a settlement. The range increases to half a mile and the area to a quarter-mile burst.

spells.name: Interplanar Teleport  (First World or the Universe only)
spells.text:
Requirements You have a planar key for the destination plane, used as a locus

---

You and your allies traverse the barriers between planes of existence. The targets move to another plane, such as the Plane of Fire, the Netherworld, or the Outer Rifts. You must know the destination plane exists and use a magic planar key created from material from that plane as a locus for the spell. While the planar keys for most prominent planes are uncommon, just like the spell interplanar teleport, more obscure planes and demiplanes often have rare or possibly even unique planar keys.

The spell is highly imprecise, and you appear 1d20×25 miles from the last place one of the targets (of your choice) was located the last time that target traveled to the plane. If it's the first time traveling to a particular plane for all targets, you appear at a random location on the plane. Interplanar teleport doesn't provide a means of return travel, though casting interplanar teleport again allows you to return to your previous plane unless there are extenuating circumstances.

spells.name: Truespeech (Constant)
spells.text:
The target can understand all words regardless of language and also speak the languages of other creatures. When in a mixed group of creatures, each time the target speaks, it can choose a creature and speak in a language that creature understands, even if the target doesn't know what language that is.

---

Heightened (7th) The duration is 8 hours.

Swat Projectile
items.text:
Requirements The fetch behemoth must have a free hand but can Release anything as part of this reaction

Trigger The fetch behemoth is targeted by a physical ranged attack

---
Effect The fetch behemoth gains a +4 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack. If the attack misses and the projectile was made of stone, the fetch behemoth can immediately throw it back at the attacker as a rock ranged Strike.

items.name: Create Boulder
items.text: The fetch behemoth molds a boulder from primal earth and throws it as a rock Strike. A creature hit by the Strike must succeed at a DC 26 Reflex save save or be knocked Prone.

text:
A fetch behemoth is much larger than a stalker and forms from the soul of a Large fey or humanoid.

---
A fetch is a twisted, deviant simulacrum of a humanoid creature that exists or existed at one point on the Universe. While there are rumors of fetches who are reflections of beings from other planes, if such exist, they must still be duplicates of a sapient creature. A fetch can manifest spontaneously when a powerful person undergoes a significant emotional event or dies, either while in the First World or in an area significantly influenced by that plane. However, they've also been created by potent entities like the Eldest to torment and vex those who've annoyed them. While a fetch manifests from a soul's "reflection," and as such bears a striking resemblance to that soul's appearance, they have no true memories of their own. They hold fragments of false remembrances from their source, as if they experienced them in a half-remembered dream—which ensures the fetch is enraged by and jealous of their original.

A fetch is similar in appearance to the creature whose soul spawned them, except that they often possess fey-like features such as pointed ears, plant elements, or supernatural grace. A fetch who seeks to impersonate a still-living source must take care to hide these features and manifest a fetch weapon that their living template wields.

When a fetch dies, they fade away along with all of their manifested items into a bloom of plant life, their soul instantly recycled into the First World, leaving behind a patch of weeds and thorny flowers roughly in the shape they held while alive.
